title: Microsoft Intune: new enrollment policies experience for iOS/iPadOS automated device enrollment
summary: Hold: the briefing makes Company Portal deployment sound necessary for user-affinity enrollment, although Microsoft says it is optional with just-in-time registration. It also leaves the sovereign-cloud restriction unresolved despite Microsoft's published mapping of GCC High and DoD to Azure Government, and needs corrections to a navigation path and permission requirements.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Intune's new iOS/iPadOS ADE enrollment policies experience.
claims.quote: Microsoft Intune: New enrollment policies experience for iOS/iPadOS ADE

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: Learn documents Enrollment policies under Enrollment program tokens as the updated creation experience replacing older Profiles.
claims.quote: This article reflects the updated policy creation experience (Enrollment program tokens > Enrollment policies) for devices going through automated device enrollment. The older experience (Enrollment program tokens > Profiles) differs and will eventually be retired.

claims.claim: The new experience applies automatically to newly created policies, supporting defaultState on for this redesign.
claims.quote: All newly created enrollment policies for iOS/iPadOS/macOS will automatically be part of the new experience. Existing enrollment profiles won't be affected.

claims.claim: Existing enrollment profiles remain editable.
claims.quote: Existing enrollment profiles can be deleted, edited, assigned to devices, and viewed. Their device assignments will not be affected or changed.

claims.claim: New enrollment profiles cannot be created in the old Profiles experience.
claims.quote: New enrollment profiles within Profiles cannot and should not be created.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Creation or assignment of a new policy never automatically sends the Company Portal app.
claims.quote: With new enrollment policies, the Company Portal application will never be sent down automatically from the creation or assignment of the enrollment policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn says the Company Portal single app mode option is unsupported and will soon be removed.
claims.quote: The Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication option is no longer supported and will soon be removed. This option must be set to No.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The blog says the new experience has no Company Portal authentication method.
claims.quote: there'll be no Company Portal authentication method or automatic deployment of the Company Portal application

claims.claim: Learn still lists Company Portal and Setup Assistant with modern authentication as options, in disagreement with the blog.
claims.quote: Your options: Company Portal; Setup Assistant with modern authentication

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn recommends Setup Assistant with modern authentication and JIT registration for iOS/iPadOS ADE with user affinity.
claims.quote: We recommend Setup Assistant with modern authentication with just-in-time (JIT) registration for iOS/iPadOS ADE with user affinity.

claims.claim: Learn states that support for Setup Assistant (legacy) ended with the October 2026, 2610 service release.
claims.quote: Intune has ended support for Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication for ADE with user affinity with the October 2026 (2610) service release.

claims.claim: The blog's April 2026 update gives service release 2606, end of June, as the iOS/iPadOS ETA.
claims.quote: 04/30/26: Updated post with new ETAs - 2606 (end of June) for iOS/iPadOS and macOS, and 2604 (end of April) for visionOS and tvOS.

claims.claim: Learn says the old experience will receive no new features.
claims.quote: The older experience won't receive new features, so be sure to create new policies under Enrollment policies.

claims.claim: Some older user-affinity profiles automatically sent the Company Portal app.
claims.quote: Previously within enrollment profiles, the Company Portal app was sent down automatically to devices with the creation of Setup Assistant with modern authentication and Company Portal authentication profiles.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: User-affinity enrollments that previously received Company Portal now need explicit Company Portal app deployment.
claims.quote: Sending the Company Portal app to ADE devices with user device affinity (optional) - iOS/iPadOS only. For Setup Assistant with modern authentication, the Company Portal is no longer required because of Just in Time registration and compliance Remediation
claims.fix: Replace the implication of mandatory deployment in Why it matters, the Before rollout checklist and the risk rationale with: 'If you still need the Company Portal app, deploy it explicitly through Intune; new policies do not send it automatically. Company Portal is optional for enrollment with Setup Assistant with modern authentication and JIT registration.' The cited blog states both points.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn says to deploy Company Portal through Intune rather than installing the App Store version on ADE devices.
claims.quote: When using automated device enrollment (ADE), deploy the Intune Company Portal app through Intune — not through the App Store.

claims.claim: Without enrollment time grouping, devices can take up to eight hours after enrollment to receive all apps and policies.
claims.quote: It can take up to 8 hours post enrollment for devices to receive all apps and policies.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new data access introduced by this experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Intune new iOS iPadOS ADE enrollment policies experience data access licensing separate price meter. Read roadmap, ADE setup, enrollment time grouping and the new-experience blog; no new data-access mechanism is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[0]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Enrollment time grouping adds enrolling devices to a selected static Microsoft Entra security group.
claims.quote: On the Device group tab, optionally select a Microsoft Entra security group to use for enrollment time grouping. Only static Microsoft Entra security groups are available for selection.

claims.claim: Changing the group's device membership changes the apps and policies the devices receive.
claims.quote: If you remove a device from the group, Microsoft Intune reevaluates policy configurations and forces the device to check in to obtain new configurations.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Intune Provisioning Client must be an owner of the enrollment time grouping security group.
claims.quote: To configure enrollment time grouping, you must add the Intune Provisioning Client as an owner of the security group.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Choosing the enrollment time grouping group requires the enrollment time device membership assignment permission in a custom RBAC role under Enrollment programs.
claims.quote: To configure this setting, you must have the enrollment time device membership assignment permission in a custom RBAC role (under Enrollment programs).

claims.claim: Adding Intune Provisioning Client as group owner needs a Microsoft Entra Group Administrator or an existing group owner.
claims.quote: you must be a Microsoft Entra Group Administrator (or hold the microsoft.directory/groups/owners/update permission), or be an existing owner of the security group.
claims.fix: Replace the role requirement with: 'Adding the Intune Provisioning Client as group owner requires a Microsoft Entra Group Administrator, an account holding microsoft.directory/groups/owners/update, or an existing owner of the security group.' This is the complete requirement at https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-enrollment/setup-time-grouping.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Await final configuration is Yes by default in new enrollment policies.
claims.quote: Yes is the default setting for new enrollment policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Await final configuration locks the end-user experience while device configuration policies install.
claims.quote: Enable a locked experience at the end of Setup Assistant to ensure your most critical device configuration policies are installed on the device. The end-user experience locks while users await final configurations.

claims.claim: Setup Assistant and Intune enforce neither a minimum nor a maximum wait during final configuration.
claims.quote: Setup Assistant and Microsoft Intune don't enforce a minimum or maximum time limit during this portion of setup.

claims.claim: Most devices in Microsoft's product validation were released within 15 minutes.
claims.quote: During product validation, most devices we tested were released and able to access the home screen within 15 minutes.

claims.claim: Changed enrollment policy settings require a factory reset and reactivation to reach assigned devices, except the device name template.
claims.quote: the new settings won't take effect on assigned devices until devices are reset back to factory settings and reactivated. The device name template setting is the only setting you can change that doesn't require a factory reset to take effect.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A synced Apple device without an assigned enrollment policy fails enrollment when turned on for setup.
claims.quote: If a device you synced from Apple isn't assigned an enrollment policy and someone turns it on to set it up, enrollment fails.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn recommends setting a default enrollment policy.
claims.quote: We recommend that you set a default enrollment policy as soon as possible so that as devices sync from Apple Business or Apple School Manager, and then turn on, they can enroll correctly through automated device enrollment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The blog warns that deleting an old enrollment profile stops enforcement of its device rename.
claims.quote: If you delete an old enrollment profile, the device rename is no longer enforced (that is if someone changes the device name).

claims.claim: Learn lists the missing Remove option for an existing policy's enrollment time grouping group as a known issue.
claims.quote: When editing an existing enrollment policy under Enrollment policies, the Remove option for the enrollment time grouping (ETG) group isn't available.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The experience is inside the licensed Intune service; any benefiting user or device needs an Intune licence, supporting licensing model included.
claims.quote: An Intune license is required for any user or device that benefits directly or indirectly from the Microsoft Intune service, including access through a Microsoft API.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Most organisations get Intune in a Microsoft 365 bundle, with E3, E5 and E7 given as examples.
claims.quote: Most organizations get Intune as part of a Microsoft 365 bundle (such as Microsoft 365 E3, E5, or E7) rather than buying these plans directly.

claims.claim: The setup page covers new or wiped iOS/iPadOS devices bought through Apple Business or Apple School Manager.
claims.quote: New or wiped iOS/iPadOS devices purchased from Apple Business or Apple School Manager.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence, price or meter for this enrollment policies experience is published in the relevant documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Intune iOS iPadOS ADE new Enrollment policies licensing price meter enrollment time grouping; new iOS iPadOS ADE enrollment policies experience data access licensing separate price meter. Opened Intune licensing, ADE setup, enrollment time grouping and the new-experience blog.

claims.claim: Learn instructs admins deploying Company Portal to deploy it as a required VPP app with device licensing.
claims.quote: Deploy the app as a required VPP app with device licensing.

claims.claim: Learn warns that insufficient Company Portal licences for a VPP token block device enrollment.
claims.quote: Devices will be blocked from enrolling if there aren't enough Company Portal licenses for a VPP token or if the token expires.

claims.claim: The limit is 1,000 enrollment policies per enrollment token.
claims.quote: There's a limit of 1,000 enrollment policies per enrollment token.

claims.claim: Learn excludes enrollment time grouping for Apple ADE policies from some sovereign clouds, including Azure operated by 21Vianet and Azure Government.
claims.quote: Enrollment time grouping for Apple automated device enrollment policies isn't available in some sovereign cloud environments, including Azure operated by 21Vianet and Azure Government.

claims.claim: How the Azure Government exclusion applies to GCC High and DoD is not stated.
claims.quote: The Intune GCC High and DoD offerings are built on the Microsoft Azure Government Cloud. Government cloud: This service is also known as GCC High or DoD.
claims.fix: Replace the unresolved caveat in Scope with: 'The enrollment time grouping page excludes Apple ADE enrollment time grouping in Azure Government. Microsoft's Intune government service description places GCC High and DoD in Azure Government, so this restriction covers those deployments even though the roadmap lists them.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/fundamentals/government-service and remove the corresponding Open questions bullet.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, inventory bullet
claims.claim: The inventory route is Enrollment program tokens > token > Profiles.
claims.quote: Existing enrollment profiles will remain in Devices > Enrollment > Apple > Enrollment program tokens > select a token > Profiles.
claims.fix: Replace the part-way-in inventory route with 'Microsoft Intune admin center > Devices > Device onboarding > Enrollment > Apple mobile > Enrollment program tokens > token > Profiles'. The current prefix is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-enrollment/apple/setup-automated-ios and the Profiles destination at the cited blog.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review or configure controls that have no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Decide the authentication method; deploy the Company Portal app as a required app; grant a policy author ... permission; set one as the default; Review Await final configuration; Review the Enrollment time grouping failures report. Table: only the enrollment time grouping group.
claims.fix: The Before rollout authentication, Company Portal assignment and custom-role permission steps, At rollout default-policy and Await final configuration steps, and After rollout failures-report step have no corresponding controls-table rows.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk versus Risk assessment

claims.fix: Add 'except changes to the device name template' to the factory-reset statements in the At rollout pilot bullet and the risk rationale. Learn states that naming-template changes take effect at the next check-in: https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-enrollment/apple/setup-automated-ios.
